<details><summary>Nits and less certain findings (24)</summary>

**12. Short tail step reports inflated FPS/TFLOPS: latent caching drops the even-batch sampler** (`primus/backends/diffusion/trainers/benchmark.py:88`)

`_cache_encoded_batches` (on by default) rebuilds the loader with a plain `DistributedSampler`/`DataLoader(drop_last=False)`, discarding `EvenSizeBatchSampler`. 5 samples at batch 4 give batch sizes `[4, 1]`, while FPS still uses the configured batch size and TFLOPS reuses the first step's FLOPs, so the short tail step reports inflated numbers. This also makes `dataloader_even_batches` dead; keep the even-batch sampler on the cached path.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: `_cache_encoded_batches` iterates `self.dataloader`, which for flux-dev is the `EvenSizeBatchSampler` loader (`BENCHMARK_TRAINER` sets `dataloader_even_batches: True`), so the cached list is already padded to a multiple of the batch size. Running the real sampler on head: 5 samples at batch 4 cache 8 samples and the rebuilt loader yields [4, 4]; 7 at batch 3 yields [3, 3, 3]._

**13. Fused RoPE cache keeps GPU tensors pinned and may return stale values; inputs under-validated** (`primus/backends/diffusion/models/flux/rope_triton.py:87`)

`_shared_cos_sin` keeps a process-global cache keyed by identity and shape but not device or dtype. It is never cleared, so `pe` and fp32 cos/sin copies stay pinned on the GPU, and it returns stale values if `pe` is modified in place. `fused_rope_supported` checks only `xq`, not the `freqs_cis` device or the `xk` layout, which risks out-of-bounds reads.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: `_shared_cos_sin` caches a single entry keyed by `is freqs_cis` while holding a reference, and `pe` is rebuilt by `pe_embedder(ids)` each forward and never written in place. `apply_rope` only takes the fused path when `xq.shape == xk.shape`, `_launch` makes inputs contiguous, and `fused_rope_supported` checks `freqs_cis` dims 0/1/3 against `x`, so no out-of-bounds or stale read is reachable._

**14. FLUX.1-dev and T5-XXL re-downloaded: HF cache fallback uses `~/cache` instead of `~/.cache`** (`primus/backends/diffusion/utils/download.py:55`)

With `PRIMUS_HF_HOME`/`HF_HOME` unset, `huggingface_home()` returns `~/cache/huggingface` (no dot), and it also overrides an explicit `HF_HOME` that equals `$DATA_PATH/huggingface`. Existing caches are bypassed, so FLUX.1-dev (~24GB) and T5-XXL are re-downloaded. Use `~/.cache/huggingface` and respect explicit `HF_HOME`; update the README and test that lock in the current path.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: The `~/cache/huggingface` root and skipping the runner's automatic `$DATA_PATH/huggingface` `HF_HOME` are stated in the download.py docstring, the backend README and the unit test. This is a deliberate, documented cache-location choice; an explicit `HF_HOME` or `PRIMUS_HF_HOME` is still honored._

**15. FSDP2 wrapping fixes will not reach benchmark runs: this PR copies `_apply_fsdp2`** (`primus/backends/diffusion/trainers/benchmark.py:126`)

`AMDBBenchmarkTrainer._apply_fsdp2` (148 lines) is a near-verbatim copy of `FSDP2Trainer._apply_fsdp2` (130 lines). The only additions are the `cast_frozen_modules` call, the `fsdp2_pure_low_precision` bf16 reduce default and `wrap_root.to(dtype=mp_dtype)`. Later fixes to the shared FSDP2 wrapping will not reach the benchmark trainer. Consider adding hooks to the parent method and calling `super()`.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers changing FSDP2 wrapping logic; no runtime effect today.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**16. PR titled FLUX.1-dev also adds four non-FLUX models and the video shim** (`primus/backends/diffusion/data/hf_torchvision_video_shim.py:25`)

The PR title names FLUX.1-dev, but the PR also adds sdxl, mochi-1, hunyuan-video and wan2.1-i2v benchmark support. That includes the torchvision `VideoReader` shim, which is used only when `modality == 'video'`, plus video decoding, Disney dataset entries and download and prepare branches. This appears deliberate and is covered by `test_benchmark_workloads.py`, so it is a scope and reviewability remark, not a defect. Consider retitling the PR or splitting the video models out.

**Who is affected:** Reviewers only; no runtime impact on FLUX.1-dev runs.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**17. About 300 lines of unreachable, untested utility code ship: this PR adds modules with no callers** (`primus/backends/diffusion/utils/checkpoint_convert.py:7`)

`utils/checkpoint_convert.py` (HunyuanVideo/Wan converters), `utils/checkpoint_io.py`, `utils/flops.py`, `utils/pixels.py`, `utils/helpers.py` and `sampling.sample_amdb_sdxl_sigmas` have no importers in `primus/`, `runner/` or `tests/`, and no tests. That is roughly 300 lines of untested dead code, part of it for models outside this PR's FLUX scope. The `torch.library` op in `flops.py` is never registered because nothing imports the module. Delete these files, or land them together with their consumers and tests.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers; no runtime path reaches these modules.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**18. MI355X benchmark numbers not comparable to MI300X/MI325X: this PR's MI355X config overrides optimizer defaults** (`primus/backends/diffusion/argument_builder.py:476`)

`BENCHMARK_TRAINER` is documented as matching AMDiffusionBenchmark (lr 1e-5, constant, `max_grad_norm` 0). The MI355X config overrides to lr 1e-4, `max_grad_norm` 1.0 and 5 warmup steps, so the grad-norm collective runs inside the timed step and cross-platform numbers are not comparable. The SDXL `warmup_steps` 100 comment is also stale.

**Who is affected:** Anyone comparing FLUX.1-dev benchmark numbers from the MI355X config with those from the MI300X/MI325X configs.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**19. Host RAM grows with dataset size under default `cache_latents`: this PR caches all encodings on CPU** (`primus/backends/diffusion/trainers/benchmark.py:66`)

With `cache_latents` on (the default), `_cache_encoded_batches` keeps every encoded sample of the rank's shard in host RAM before training. That is the latents plus the 512-token T5 encodings, about 4 MB per sample in bf16. Host memory therefore grows linearly with dataset size. This is deliberate, to match AMDiffusionBenchmark's cached-latent runs, and can be disabled with `cache_latents: false`. The `encode()`-returns-None fallback is unreachable, and the cached tensors are not pinned, so no other change is needed.

**Who is affected:** Users running `flux-dev` benchmarks on large raw datasets with the default `cache_latents=True`.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**20. `black --check` fails on the registry: this PR adds builders with one blank line** (`primus/backends/diffusion/registry.py:106`)

Only one blank line precedes `MODEL_BUILDERS` after the new `_build_amdb_benchmark_trainer`, so the repo's pinned `black` 24.8.0 pre-commit hook reformats `registry.py`. The new builders are also added by mutating `MODEL_BUILDERS`/`DATASET_BUILDERS`/`TRAINER_BUILDERS` after the literals instead of listing them inline. Add the blank line and list `flux-dev`, `amdb` and `amdb_benchmark` in the dict literals.

**Who is affected:** Contributors running pre-commit or a lint CI step on this file.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**21. Even-batch padding repeats samples and ignores `dataloader_drop_last`, undocumented and untested** (`primus/backends/diffusion/trainers/base.py:149`)

Tail padding repeats rank-local samples, giving them extra gradient weight and counting them in FPS. A shard smaller than the batch is padded entirely by repetition (`range(1), 4` gives `[[0,0,0,0]]`), and `dataloader_drop_last` is ignored. Document this and test batch > dataset, an empty sampler, and `__len__`.

_An independent check of the code found this probably does not apply: The sampler docstring (base.py:149) and the `BENCHMARK_TRAINER` comment in argument_builder.py both state that the short tail is padded from the rank-local front, that FPS uses the configured batch size, and that MLPerf mode bypasses the sampler. Ignoring `dataloader_drop_last` is inherent to an option whose purpose is to never drop or shorten batches, so this is a documented design choice._

**22. Second checkpoint loader added alongside `train_utils` loaders; omits explicit `weights_only=True`** (`primus/backends/diffusion/utils/checkpoint_io.py:18`)

`checkpoint_io.load_state_dict` largely duplicates `utils/train_utils.py` `load_state_dict*`. Its additions are the nested `state_dict`/`model`/`module` unwrap and sorted glob ordering, which could live in the existing helper. Unlike `load_state_dict_from_bin`, it does not pass `weights_only=True` explicitly. On torch >= 2.6 (torch 2.10 here) that is already the default, so the omission matters only on older torch.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers of the diffusion checkpoint loading helpers.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**23. Frame-list video clips darkened by double normalization in `videos_to_tensor` (latent, no callers)** (`primus/backends/diffusion/utils/pixels.py:90-98`)

On the frame-list path, `_frame_tensor` already maps to [-1, 1], then the clip is rescaled again when `min() >= 0`. Pixels of 200 become 0.1373 instead of 0.5686, so results depend on the container type. Skip the second rescale for already-normalized frames (currently latent, as there are no callers).

**Origin:** latent

**Who is affected:** No current user; only a future caller that passes videos as frame lists to `decode_host_pixels`/`videos_to_tensor`.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**24. Prepare hook crashes with `AttributeError` when `model.encoder` is null or a string** (`runner/helpers/hooks/train/pretrain/diffusion/prepare.py:173`)

In `_validate_benchmark_model`, `encoder_cfg = model_cfg.get('encoder', {}) or model.get('encoder', {})` falls back to the raw top-level `model.encoder` whenever `model.config.encoder` is empty. `_stage_benchmark_downloads` stores `{}` there when nothing was configured or staged. If the YAML also sets a top-level `model.encoder: null` or a string, the later `.get` calls raise `AttributeError` instead of a clear validation failure. Normalize it the way `_stage_benchmark_downloads` does (`or {}` plus an `isinstance(dict)` check). The same fallback idiom already exists on the base for `wan` and FLUX raw.

**Who is affected:** Users of the new sdxl, mochi-1, hunyuan-video or wan2.1-i2v benchmark configs who write a malformed top-level `model.encoder` and use a non-synthetic, non-.pt dataset.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**25. Converter docstring promises lossless conversion but Wan silently drops `attn2.norm_added_q.weight`** (`primus/backends/diffusion/utils/checkpoint_convert.py:10`)

The docstring says tensors are only renamed, re-fused or re-ordered, but `wan_diffusers_to_native` skips `.attn2.norm_added_q.weight` keys. Update the docstring to say Diffusers-only parameters with no native counterpart are dropped.

**Who is affected:** Readers of `checkpoint_convert.py`; the converters currently have no callers in the repo.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**26. FLUX config comment cites UNet convolutions FLUX.1-dev does not have** (`examples/diffusion/configs/MI355X/benchmark_flux_dev-posttrain.yaml:7`)

All three `benchmark_flux_dev-posttrain.yaml` files say MIOpen FAST mode 'picks slower VAE and UNet convolutions', but FLUX.1-dev has no UNet. The comment looks copied from an SDXL config; drop 'and UNet'.

**Who is affected:** Readers of the MI300X/MI325X/MI355X `benchmark_flux_dev-posttrain.yaml` configs.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**27. Users cannot discover `BENCHMARK_DENOISER_ONLY`, which skips encoder/VAE staging** (`primus/backends/diffusion/utils/download.py:323`)

`BENCHMARK_DENOISER_ONLY=1` silently skips encoder/VAE staging and the encoder prefetch. It is not mentioned in the module or function docstrings or the README, which list the other benchmark env vars. Document it in the README.

**Who is affected:** Users of the AMDB benchmark prepare hook who want or accidentally set `BENCHMARK_DENOISER_ONLY=1`.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**28. README batch-size table does not say values are default `LOCAL_BATCH_SIZE`** (`examples/diffusion/README.md:134`)

The `| Workload | MI300X / MI325X | MI355X |` table (10 / 16) follows a learning-rate paragraph and doesn't say the values are the default `LOCAL_BATCH_SIZE`. Add an intro line or rename the columns.

**Who is affected:** Readers of the examples/diffusion README choosing a FLUX.1-dev benchmark config.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**29. Sigma grid rebuilt on every training step; negligible cost** (`primus/backends/diffusion/models/flux/train_pipeline.py:181`)

The `amdb_logit_normal` branch calls `sample_shifted_logit_normal_sigmas` without `sigma_grid`, so `amdb_flow_sigma_grid` rebuilds the same 1000-entry FP32 CPU table on every training step. The cost is microseconds (one `arange` and two elementwise ops), and the function-local import is just a `sys.modules` lookup after the first call. This is a tidy-up, not a measurable throughput issue: optionally cache the grid once and pass `sigma_grid=`.

**Who is affected:** FLUX training runs with `timestep_sampling: amdb_logit_normal` (assumed to be the AMDB benchmark configs; not checked against the config files).

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**30. Timestep-sampling predicate duplicated and negated, risking unset or double-computed `sigmas`** (`primus/backends/diffusion/models/flux/train_pipeline.py:200`)

`dit.training and self.cfg.timestep_sampling == 'amdb_logit_normal'` appears at line 176 and again negated at line 200, so the two checks can drift out of sync. Compute the predicate once or restructure the branches.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers editing the FLUX train_pipeline timestep branches.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**31. `_log_step` recomputes global batch size inline instead of `_global_batch_size()`** (`primus/backends/diffusion/trainers/benchmark.py:326`)

`_log_step` computes `per_device_train_batch_size * grad_accum_steps * data_parallel_world_size` inline, although the same file already uses `self._global_batch_size()`. Call the helper instead.

**Who is affected:** Users of the AMDB FLUX.1-dev benchmark trainer (benchmark_flux_dev-posttrain configs).

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**32. Missing FLOPs converted None→0.0→None redundantly** (`primus/backends/diffusion/trainers/benchmark.py:512`)

When `total_flops` is None, it is converted to 0.0 for `benchmark_step_rates` and the result is then mapped back to None at line 512. Set `step_tflops = None` directly, or let the helper accept Optional.

**Who is affected:** Users of the AMDB FLUX.1-dev benchmark trainer (benchmark_flux_dev-posttrain configs).

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**33. Extra fp32 copy of q/k per block per step: this PR's RMSNorm casts twice** (`primus/backends/diffusion/models/flux/layers.py:75`)

The new eps path of `RMSNorm.forward` calls `x.float()` twice, materialising two fp32 copies of q/k (and saving them for backward) in every Double/SingleStreamBlock. The FLUX.1-dev benchmark registration sets `qk_norm_eps=1e-6` and `compile_transformer_blocks` defaults to False, so nothing fuses it. Compute `xf = x.float()` once, as BFL's reference does. Note that `F.rms_norm` would apply the weight before the downcast, which changes numerics relative to the BFL ordering this code mirrors.

**Who is affected:** Users of the AMDB FLUX.1-dev benchmark trainer (benchmark_flux_dev-posttrain configs).

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**34. Broken `PRIMUS_FLUX_TRITON_ROPE` dispatch in `apply_rope` would still pass tests** (`primus/backends/diffusion/models/flux/math.py:56`)

The GPU test calls `fused_apply_rope` directly and no test sets `PRIMUS_FLUX_TRITON_ROPE=1`, so breaking `_fused_rope_enabled` or the dispatch would still pass. Also run `apply_rope` with the variable set and compare against eager.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers relying on CI to catch regressions in the opt-in `PRIMUS_FLUX_TRITON_ROPE=1` RoPE dispatch.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**35. Benchmark could silently use default q/k norm eps: `qk_norm_eps` plumbing untested** (`primus/backends/diffusion/models/flux/layers.py:98`)

`qk_norm_eps`, threaded through `FluxParams`, `DoubleStreamBlock` and `SingleStreamBlock` into `QKNorm`, has no test. Build the tiny flux model with `qk_norm_eps=1e-6` and assert the eps on the block norms.

**Who is affected:** FLUX.1-dev benchmark runs whose `build_flux_dev_benchmark` defaults `qk_norm_eps` to `1e-6`; any regression in threading it through would go unnoticed.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

</details>
